tldr: Tong, Cheng, Tong, Harhay, and Li's identification equations are taken as published input for the adjacent \(G=(0,1,1)\) survivor contrast.  The decision-theoretic contribution first lifts Evans, Hansen, and Stark's symmetric monotone-likelihood-ratio bounded-shift theorem to every outward radial multiplier \(\kappa\ge1\): when \(\tau\le2q\), the exact minimax expected length remains \(2\int_0^\tau F(q-u)\,du\).  The equal-projected-variance Gaussian specialization yields \(|\Delta_0^\nu-\Delta_1^\nu|\,2v\int_0^\tau\Phi(c-u)\,du\), and the proved studentized causal interval attains this value uniformly over the stated shrinking nuisance neighborhoods.  Unknown total stratum mass therefore has zero minimax length cost relative to the shell \(s=\rho\).
gap: Tong et al. (2025), Section 2, Equation (2), and Section 3.1, Equations (3)--(4), already identify the multi-arm principal contrast, and their Theorem 1 supports regular efficient estimation. Published bounded-normal theory fixes the scalar location geometry. Neither literature gives an exact confidence-length frontier when the already identified adjacent principal mass is local to zero and its total magnitude is unknown.
fill: Using Tong et al.'s identification functional without claiming it as new, the project proves the unknown-radius Gaussian lift, derives the original-sample lower bound by continuum likelihood-ratio tests, and constructs a uniformly valid deterministic causal interval using studentized cell contrasts and bounded-outcome enlargement.
